Maintenance Report — MNT-0085-008

Asset: WELL-0085 (SW-24 Well 085, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 13 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 16 Apr 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 84 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0085-0075 on 2024-04-11 Report written: 18 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0085-0075 showed the wellhead at 24.4 °C with the air at 18.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0085-031

Asset: WELL-0085 (SW-24 Well 085, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 22 Sep 2026 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 424 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0085-0197 on 2026-09-03 Report written: 24 Sep 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0085-0197 showed the wellhead at 33.8 °C with the air at 34.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point. This is corrective repair number 7 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 189 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 151 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0085-031 (WS-06).
